reference.title: KC1 prediction API reference
reference.shortdesc: The KC1 API serves the project's defect-prediction model over HTTP. Send the 21 static code metrics of one software module, and it returns whether the model flags the module as defective, with the probability and the threshold behind the decision.

section.p: FastAPI's test client recorded every request and response on this page on 19 November 2026, against the model that the project's own trainer produced. The test client calls the application in the same process, so the recording needed no server and no port. The trained model reproduces the model card: logistic regression with balanced class weights, a threshold of 0.50, and F1 0.500 on the 243 test modules.

section.title: At a glance

strow.stentry: http://127.0.0.1:8000, when you start the API with the project's Docker Compose file. The Compose file publishes the port on this computer only.
JSON in and JSON out. Send Content-Type: application/json.
None. The API has no sign-in and no keys. Keep it on 127.0.0.1, as the Compose file does, or put an authenticating gateway in front of it.
None. The API doesn't limit requests.
Doesn't apply. Each call returns one object.
OpenAPI 3.1, served by the API at /openapi.json, with Swagger UI at /docs and ReDoc at /redoc.

section.p: Download the OpenAPI description as the API serves it, or every recorded request and response.

section.title: Endpoints

strow.stentry: Names the API and the model it serves.
Says whether the API has loaded the model, with its name, its threshold, and the number of features it expects.
Predicts whether one module is defective.

section.p: None of the endpoints takes a path parameter or a query parameter.

section.title: GET /health
section.p: Check that the API is up and has loaded the model, before you send predictions.

strow.stentry: true when the model loaded at startup. The API doesn't start without a model, so it's always true in practice.
The name of the candidate the trainer selected.
The probability at and above which a module is called defective.

section.p: GET / returns a shorter form of the same: {"message": "Group 6 KC1 Software Defect Prediction API", "model": "Logistic balanced"}.

section.title: POST /predict
section.p: Send the metrics of one module. The API answers with one prediction.

section.title: Request body
section.p: A JSON object with exactly these 21 fields, each a finite number. A field that is missing, a field that isn't on the list, and a value that isn't a number are all refused. The definitions follow the PROMISE repository's description of KC1.

strow.stentry: McCabe's count of lines of code
Halstead's total of operators and operands
Halstead program level, about 1 divided by d
Lines with both code and a comment

section.p: Three names contain parentheses: v(g), ev(g) and iv(g). The API also accepts them as v_g, ev_g and iv_g, which suit tools that don't accept parentheses in a name. The recorded responses are the same either way.

section.title: Response

strow.stentry: 1 when the model flags the module as defective, 0 when it doesn't.
Defective or Non-defective, the same decision in words.
The model's probability that the module is defective, from 0 to 1. It is null only for a model without probabilities, which the selected model isn't.
The probability at and above which prediction is 1.
The model that made the prediction.

section.p: A flagged module, recorded the same way, comes back as {"prediction": 1, "label": "Defective", "defect_probability": 0.6756835241062081, "threshold": 0.5, "model": "Logistic balanced"}.

section.title: Errors

strow.stentry: A field is missing, a field isn't one of the 21, a value isn't a number, or the body isn't a JSON object.
detail: one entry for each problem, with its type, its location loc, a message msg and the input that caused it.
The path doesn't exist, such as /predictions.
The path exists but takes another method, such as GET /predict.
A number too large for a 64-bit float, such as 1e999. This is a known fault: see Troubleshoot the KC1 API.
Internal Server Error, as plain text

section.p: A request that sends only loc gets one entry for each of the 20 missing fields. Here is the first one.

section.title: Code examples
section.p: Here is the same request in Python, with the requests library.
section.codeblock:
import requests
metrics = { "loc": 25, "v(g)": 3, "ev(g)": 1, "iv(g)": 3, "n": 58, "v": 254.75, "l": 0.11, "d": 9.35, "i": 27.25, "e": 2381.95, "b": 0.08, "t": 132.33, "lOCode": 21, "lOComment": 0, "lOBlank": 2, "locCodeAndComment": 0, "uniq_Op": 11, "uniq_Opnd": 10, "total_Op": 41, "total_Opnd": 17, "branchCount": 5, } response = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:8000/predict", json=metrics, timeout=10) response.raise_for_status() result = response.json() print(result["label"], round(result["defect_probability"], 3))
section.p: Run against the API, with the test client in place of the network, it prints Non-defective 0.392. The same request in JavaScript uses fetch, in a module or an async function.
